newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market slow amid weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market slow amid weak demand.

text.p: Croatian money market trade remained slow amid a low demand for kuna funds, dealers said on Tuesday.
"The money market is slow today. There had been more kuna on offer than actual deals closed, as lenders and borrowers could not agree on terms," a dealer told Reuters.

Fresh trade totalled 17 million kuna of which two thirds were call money loans mostly granted at an unchanged rate of 10.5 percent with one deal being struck at eight percent, a foreign bank acting as the lender.
One 30-day loan was struck at 15 percent and there was a two-month loan granted at 20 percent, up two percent from Monday.
There was no overnight trade on Monday with banks' accounts totalling 384 million kuna. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
